assertions: Two calls on the same PrefectScheduler overlap at a barrier using distinct runtimes and run IDs; one succeeds while one fails without mixing outputs, reports, flow IDs, or task IDs.
Prefect flow-run IDs remain distinct and observed task-run IDs parse as UUIDs rather than ETLantic fallback identifiers.
Run-level and step-level timeout policies cause the outer Prefect flow call to fail and preserve an unsuccessful ETLantic report.
CancellationPolicy(cooperative=False) and bounded-abandonment requests are rejected by scheduler analysis with PMSCHED103.
Legacy discovery, conformance, report metadata, direct profile execution, and adaptive-plan rejection remain covered.
Selecting the normalized step retained its source dependency and excluded the downstream load.
A fail-once transformation used the ETLantic retry policy for exactly two attempts while Prefect task retries remained disabled.
Cancelling an active PrefectScheduler.execute caller stopped the in-flight node promptly and preserved a CANCELLED ETLantic report with the actual Prefect flow-run ID.
Setting an active flow to CANCELLING through the Prefect API stopped the in-flight node promptly and preserved a CANCELLED ETLantic report.
Three independent ready branches reached peak concurrency two under Profile(concurrency=2), despite request metadata asking for three; all branch outputs and the report succeeded.

Hostile Prefect defaults enabling three retries, caching, and result persistence did not alter ETLantic-owned two-attempt retry behavior, did not reuse cached results on a second run, and did not persist flow/task result data or task cache keys.

runtime.prefect_server: Prefect temporary test server with its own SQLite test database

fingerprints.etlantic_prefect_source_sha256_method: SHA-256 over sorted package-relative Python and JSON paths and file bytes, with NUL separators

limitations: This source-checkout run is local proof; the installed-wheel candidate matrix is the release qualification gate.
The temporary SQLite Prefect server is not the self-hosted Prefect/PostgreSQL release topology.
